claims.text: Low-temperature annealing reduces chemical and structural inhomogeneities in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys.
Annealing narrows the distribution of local exchange interactions.
The distribution of local exchange interactions governs the magnetostructural transition in FeMnNiGeSi alloys.
Homogenization should smooth the magnetocaloric response and reduce hysteresis under low applied fields.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy has a disordered microstructure.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy has heterogeneous chemical short-range order.
Microstructural disorder and heterogeneous chemical short-range order lead to a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Annealing below the order-disorder transition for a calibrated duration can promote homogenization without complete phase transformation.
An annealing window exists that avoids full diffusion or phase separation while relieving internal stresses.
The relevant structural mediator is the degree and uniformity of chemical short-range order and residual stress at grain boundaries and interfaces.
Annealing relieves internal stresses in the alloy.
Annealing reduces compositional fluctuations in the alloy.
Reduced stress and compositional fluctuations narrow the distribution of magnetostructural transition barriers.
Homogenized exchange interactions reduce hysteretic losses during magnetic cycling.
Annealed samples should have lower coercivity and a smaller magnetic-hysteresis loop area than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples should exhibit a more gradual magnetization change and a broader, less abrupt magnetocaloric response.
Annealing may modestly reduce the peak magnetic entropy change.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films have limited heat-exchange rates because of a low surface-to-volume ratio.
The predictions are restricted to similarly deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys and may not transfer to arc-melted or otherwise structurally distinct bulk forms.
